name: Billy Caldwell (Sauganash), who came to Chicago on 16 August 1812
head: caldwell_billy
review_note: review_required: a named Native man of the Chicago country in August 1812, the eve of the attack on the garrison and its families. touches_removal: his people were removed from Illinois after 1833. The card states what its sources say, with their tier, and stages no speech, ceremony or act of war.

present_on_scene_date.note: His card says how his presence is known.

associated_with.note: Not his home: Wau-Bun brings him to the Kinzie house on the 16th, where he turned the Wabash party away. His card is found there.

not_in_this_household.note: Not drawn in the scene: he was not, or may not have been, at Chicago on the 14th.

persons.name: Billy Caldwell (Sauganash)

present_on_scene_date.note: Not at Chicago on the 14th (Andreas; Currey); Wau-Bun brings him on the 16th.

also_written: Straight Tree (his first Indian name, Andreas)
persons.note: Son of a Potawatomi mother and an Irish-born British officer, born about 1780; in 1812 with Tecumseh and the British. Andreas and Currey say he was not at the evacuation. Wau-Bun brings him across the river by canoe on the 16th, when he talked the Wabash party out of harming the Kinzies; Quaife allows the story a 'kernel of fact' at most. He later led the united bands at the 1833 treaty, went west with them in 1836, and died at Council Bluffs on 28 September 1841.
